chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said, 'Allah never ceased to be an Intender.' He said: 'The Intender cannot be except with an object of intention alongside it. Allah never ceased to be a Knower, Powerful — then He Willed.'

key_terms.صِفَةُ الْفِعْلِ: Attribute of the deed — a divine attribute that arises in relation to God's actions in time, as opposed to eternal attributes of the essence (sifat al-dhat).
key_terms.عَالِم: Knower; affirmed as an eternal attribute of God's essence.
key_terms.قَادِر: Powerful/Able; affirmed as an eternal attribute of God's essence.
key_terms.مُرَاد: The object of will or intention; the thing that is willed. The Imam argues no such co-eternal object exists.
key_terms.مُرِيد: One who wills or intends; used here to probe whether 'Willer' is an eternal divine attribute.

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq say Allah's will (irada) is not an eternal attribute?
ai.summary: A questioner poses the proposition that God has always been 'an Intender,' implying His will (irada) is an eternal attribute. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes this by pointing out that the very concept of 'intending' logically requires a co-existent object of intention — which would mean something else exists eternally alongside God, a form of implicit shirk. Instead, the Imam affirms that God's eternal attributes are Knowledge and Power; His Will arises in time in relation to specific acts, and is therefore an 'attribute of the deed' (sifat al-fi'l) rather than an eternal 'attribute of the essence' (sifat al-dhat). This is a cornerstone of Shia Imami theology on divine attributes.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Attar, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa Al Ashary, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed Al Ahwazy, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> never ceased to be an Intender?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Intender cannot happen to be except with an intention along with him. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> never ceased to be a Knower, Powerful, then Intended (Willed)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa al-Ash‘ari from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id al-Ahwazi from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Asim ibn Hamiyd who has said the following. “I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), ‘Is Allah’s will eternal?’”
He replied, Will is always with what is willed. Allah is eternally All-knowing and All-powerful and then He wills.”
